scope: Replace repeated task-specific Preview refreshes with reviewed exact-release/task consent in the existing configuration journal; preserve legacy receipts and generic pilot denial.
riskAnalysis: A consent is an owner-authenticated scoped permission record, not model authority or proof of human independent acceptance. Every paid stage still needs a fresh one-use task approval, exact runtime/source/evidence, live transactional consent validation and managed invocation proof. No provider credential or hosting settings are changed by this endpoint.

threatModel.assets: Owner authority, exact release/task identities, immutable historical receipts and financial provenance, provider credentials, revocation and cleanup.
threatModel.trustBoundaries: Owner API versus private controller proof; untrusted client selectors versus current journal/CAS; engineering transport versus generic pilot activation; automated criticism versus human acceptance.
threatModel.abuseCases: Reuse consent across tasks or workspaces, forge invocation proof, revoke between count and dispatch, disconnect while consent authentication waits, mutate historical evidence or enable generic paid workers.
threatModel.mitigations: Plan and canonical task checks, hashed immutable record, owner/workspace/runtime binding, private WeakMaps, transactional reread, early abort listeners and scoped bounded revocation, generic flags stay disabled.

defects.rootCause: Per-task configuration refresh coupled owner trial scope to deployment metadata, adding repeated builds and acknowledgement recovery.
defects.detectionGap: Consumer contracts previously assumed the legacy hosting refresh record and did not share a task-specific alternative.
defects.regression: Real offline five-stage controller, API, CAS and data-copy worker tests use v2 records while all three legacy paid flags remain false. Historical configuration/lifecycle tests pass unchanged.
defects.historicalPrevention: V1 records and completed refresh acknowledgements remain immutable. V2 uses explicit versioned consent without invented provider acknowledgements.

defects.rootCause: Initial candidate stored but did not enforce plan identity; API awaited consent before registering connection cancellation.
defects.detectionGap: Same-objective fixtures and direct controller tests did not challenge foreign plan or API disconnect during lookup.
defects.regression: Cross-plan/foreign-task denial and actual API disconnect with valid active approval assert zero provider requests and revoked authority.
defects.historicalPrevention: One shared assertConsent enforces live scope; cancellation listeners cover all awaited lookup work, with existing scoped cleanup before invocation.

rollback: Keep paid execution disabled and revoke task grants/consents. Revert runtime only through a reviewed feature successor. Preserve all v1/v2 journal records, immutable hashes, revocation events and financial evidence; do not revive consumed approvals.

negativePaths.malformed-response: Existing model schema/evidence validators unchanged. New consent validates hashes, event chain, policy pins and source scope; forged selectors fail.
negativePaths.stale-state: Expired/revoked consent and wrong plan/runtime denied; history validation remains separate from live admission.
negativePaths.concurrency: Existing CAS and serial sequence controls remain. Same consent claim is idempotent in journal; no parallel dispatch or provider retry.
negativePaths.cancellation: Operations emergency stop revokes consent; API disconnect before invocation performs bounded exact-approval revocation; existing in-run cancellation remains.
negativePaths.worker-interruption: No worker execution permissions changed. Existing data-copy cleanup and artifact evidence are exercised by five-stage fixtures.
negativePaths.api-outage: Interrupted consent lookup cannot start paid dispatch; request failure produces no automatic retry. Existing failure accounting remains.
negativePaths.authorization-denial: Non-owner, cross-workspace, cross-plan and forged private proof denied; generic initializePilot remains disabled.
negativePaths.spending-limit: Existing owner-directed billing monitoring policy unchanged; revoked/expired consent remains historical provenance without granting future paid authority.
negativePaths.partial-execution: Counting-to-dispatch revocation retains observed uncertainty, no Responses call; failed attempts revoke authority and preserve evidence.

proactiveReview.architecture: Reuse existing journal, controller, sequence, broker and transport. No competing service, credential store or orchestration layer.
proactiveReview.dependencies: No new dependencies, provider permissions, hosting infrastructure or credentials. Non-secret policy pins come from verified persisted record only.
proactiveReview.threats: Independent review challenged cross-task reuse, cached readiness, lost abort events and pre-invocation cleanup; all receive direct regressions.
proactiveReview.failureModes: Expired task cannot use consent for replacement. UI preserves same reviewed task; next task needs fresh consent and new sequence with prior sequence stopped.
proactiveReview.faultInjection: Offline actual controller and API tests cover revocation after count, foreign scope, disconnect during read, malformed API selector, emergency stop and expiry.
proactiveReview.independentChallenge: Independent Work QA and Auditor identified plan binding and abort-window defects; both corrected before publication. Static review is not authenticated business acceptance.
proactiveReview.recovery: Durable configuration history preserved; stopping revokes consent and approval while retaining accounting. No duplicate refresh operations or live paid testing in this repair.
proactiveReview.readiness: Existing da19 Browser archive qualified. New candidate has focused controller/API/UI/history tests; exact-source STRICT/Redis/CI/CodeQL/Preview/browser qualification remains required before live use.
